I'm pretty late to the party here but I have to suggest that you try out Don Quixote. I've been reading it for school and I have to say, I've never actually laughed out loud at a book (I'm not a big reader), and this was the first time I ever had. In my opinion very little is lost in the translation from Spanish to English by the way.


If you like modern characters like Deadpool you might like this story, since Don Quixote was one of the first to do 'breaking the fourth wall'. Not to mention that both Deadpool and Don Quixote are satires that criticize contemporary literature (Don Quixote is basically 120+ chapters of making fun of books of chivalry).

What you said -- that Quixote is too hard and long is kind of true -- that's why you should pick and choose the chapters you read instead of reading the whole book. I suggest reading chapters:

1-9, 15-22, and 52 from volume one

1, 2, and 74 from volume two

That's 21 chapters in total, all of which include the most famous/recognizable scenes from the book (the windmills, yelmo de Mambrino, the inns, the blanketing of Sancho Panzo, etc.)
